subject: Postcall: NovaCorp TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Patel <jane.patel@novacorp.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@novacorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Postcall: NovaCorp TCO recap & next steps

Hi Jane / Tom —

Thanks for your time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you raised:
- Token spend is the largest line item in your inference cost and is currently growing ~30% quarter-over-quarter.
- Many requests have long shared prefixes which leads to repeat compute on identical context windows.
- Real-time SLA needs make it hard to batch; that increases per-token compute cost.
- Procurement has a monthly budget target (~$25k) and needs a clear TCO comparison to move forward.

Goals we discussed:
- Reduce per-user inference cost to fit within the $25k/month cap while preserving latency SLAs.
- Identify short-term levers (batching + KV/prefix caching) and mid-term changes (quantized model variants, reserved capacity).
- Build a concise TCO model that shows payback from a reserved capacity / caching deployment.

High-level recommendations (we'll deliver a modeled TCO by EOD tomorrow):
1) Prefix/KV caching: depending on reuse, expect 30–60% effective token reduction on repeat flows.
2) Smart batching: for asynchronous flows we can combine requests and reduce overhead; even small batching windows (50–200ms) yield material per-token savings.
3) Model variant & quantization: a quantized 8-bit variant can reduce GPU cost per token 20–40% with minimal quality loss on most prompts.
4) Reserved capacity: reserve vs on-demand can yield 30–50% unit-cost savings for steady traffic.

Next steps agreed:
- We will share the NovaCorp-specific TCO workbook (attached) with assumptions and a sensitivity table.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical workshop with our Solutions Engineering team to validate caching/batching feasibility (Rafael to coordinate).
- Procurement will need a simple price/commit sheet for their review — Rafael and I will draft.

Attachments: novacorp_tco_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If any of the assumptions above are off, flag them and I'll update before the model iteration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifications before you build the model:

1) Budget constraint: procurement is targeting a hard cap of $25k/month for inference (hosted or reserved) for our initial pilot.
2) Current telemetry: we average ~5M tokens/day (combined input+output) across playground and prod; peak bursts up to ~9M/day.
3) Latency constraints: user-facing chat must stay <= 350ms P95; batchable backend jobs can tolerate up to 2s.

Can you show two scenarios in the workbook: (A) hosted with caching + batching (no commit), and (B) 6-month reserved capacity + caching? Would like to see breakouts: token unit cost, infra cost, and expected monthly spend for both.

Also, can you call out the assumptions for batching (avg batch size, added latency) and caching (cache hit rate) — those are the sensitive knobs for procurement.

Tom and I are available Thursday afternoon for the workshop.

Thanks,
Jane
Director, Product — NovaCorp
jane.patel@novacorp.com

Jane — great, thanks for the details. Attached is the first pass TCO workbook and a one-page summary (redwood_tco_calculator.pdf). Highlights and the assumptions used in the model:

Assumptions (base scenario):
- Current avg tokens/day: 5,000,000 (input+output).
- Current effective price (on-demand host) used for modeling: $0.012 per 1K tokens (this is illustrative — final pricing will be in the quote).
- Latency target for chat: P95 <= 350ms (we model a mix of low-latency and batchable traffic: 70% low-latency, 30% batchable).
- Caching hit-rate scenarios modeled: 20%, 40%, 60%.
- Batching improvements modeled as effective compute reduction (per-token) for batchable traffic; base avg batch size assumed 4 with 100–200ms aggregation window for background flows.

Model outputs (summary):
- Hosted + caching (40% hit-rate) + lightweight batching: estimated monthly spend = ~$28k (base price assumptions).
- Reserved 6-month commitment + caching (40%) + batching + quantized model variant: estimated monthly spend = ~$17k–$20k depending on commit level and exact token distribution.

Key levers and sensitivity:
- If caching hit-rate moves from 20% -> 60%, hosted spend drops ~35–45% (depends on share of repeat traffic).
- Reserved capacity discounts are multiplicative with quantization: combined impact can reduce unit cost by roughly 45–60% relative to on-demand hosted.

Recommended next steps (short-term win):
1) Pilot caching on the top 3 repeat user flows (we expect fastest impact).
2) Run a 2-week batchability test on non-real-time endpoints to validate average batch sizes.
3) Confirm procurement timeline and, if comfortable, we can produce a firm reserved capacity quote tied to your traffic profile.

Attachments: redwood_tco_calculator.pdf (pdf), novacorp_tco_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

I'll also share the workbook in Drive for collaborative comments: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C-novacorp-tco

Rafael — can you pick a time for the workshop on Thursday afternoon?

Best,
Marissa
